item.title: A Prominent Mexican Politician Says U.S. Revoked His Visa
item.description: Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, a former president’s son, lashed out at the Trump administration after he said it canceled his visa, another flashpoint in the tense U.S.-Mexico relationship.
item.dc:creator: Jack Nicas, Annie Correal and Emiliano Rodríguez Mega
item.media:description: Andrés Manuel López Beltrán is the son of Mexico’s former president Andrés Manuel López Obrador, who is still a key leader of Morena, Mexico’s dominant political party.

item.title: 8 Matisse Works, Looted from Library in Brazil, Are Recovered

item.dc:creator: John Yoon

item.media:description: A handout photo released by the São Paulo police press office showing the recovered Matisse works.

item.title: After 2 Plasma Donor Deaths, Company Pauses Clinics in Canada
item.description: Grifols, a Spanish company, said “unfounded attention” on its blood plasma business in Canada had led it to temporarily end collections at 17 clinics.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai
item.media:description: Donating plasma for Grifols at a hospital in Barcelona in 2020. The company has suspended collecting plasma in Canada because of scrutiny over two deaths.

item.title: Topos Azteca, a Mexican Volunteer Rescue Group, Helps With Rescue Efforts After Colombia Earthquake
item.description: Topos Azteca, a Mexican volunteer rescue group that works worldwide and helped after the Sept. 11 attacks, arrived in Colombia after searching for survivors in Venezuela.
item.dc:creator: Genevieve Glatsky and Federico Rios
item.media:credit: Federico Rios for The New York Times
item.media:description: A member of Topos Azteca working among the rubble on Wednesday in Cali, Colombia.

item.title: Brazil’s Disease-Fighting Mosquitoes
item.description: Our reporter, Apoorva Mandavilli, goes inside a mosquito factory in Brazil, where scientists are producing millions of mosquitoes to fight deadly tropical diseases in a warming world.
item.dc:creator: Apoorva Mandavilli, Leila Medina, Alexandra Ostasiewicz, Joey Sendaydiego and Tuna Mayer

item.title: A City Mobilizes Against a Stubborn Health Threat: Mosquitoes
item.description: The city of Belém in northern Brazil was overwhelmed by an outbreak of dengue two years ago. An all-out municipal effort has reduced cases and may offer lessons to American cities.
item.dc:creator: Apoorva Mandavilli and Alessandro Falco
item.media:description: A health worker discarding water from a larvicide dissemination unit in Belém, Brazil, last month.

item.title: Come for the Cottage in ‘Heated Rivalry.’ Stay for Everything Else.
item.description: The chance to see the hideaway from the hit queer hockey romance lured me to Canada’s cottage country. But it was the glistening lakes and weep-worthy sunsets that won me over.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Bahr and Brendan George Ko
item.media:description: One of the many attractions in the Muskoka region of Ontario: the free Tuesday-evening water-skiing show on Lake Muskoka in Bala.

item.title: Trump Tariffs Force Some Canadian Companies to Move South of the Border

item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: Turning nearly pure copper into electrical wires is one of the first stages of production at Northern Cables in Brockville, Ontario.

item.title: Before Trump’s Catering Container Ruse, Other Presidents Obscured Risky Travel Plans

item.title: As Death Toll From Colombia Earthquake Rises to at Least 181, Rescuers Hunt for Survivors

item.title: What to Know About the Cuban Mafia in Quintana Roo
item.description: A group of Cuban men in Mexico was charged with smuggling people to the United States. One of its leaders said Raúl Castro’s grandson helped, according to interviews and court records.

item.title: How Raúl Castro’s Grandson, Raúl G. Rodríguez Castro, Became a Power Broker

item.title: What We Know About the Earthquake in Colombia

item.title: Colombia Quake Chases Teenage Venezuelan Brothers From Their New Home

item.title: Flight Is Canceled After a Child Refuses to Be Seated
item.description: Passengers aboard a Porter Airlines plane headed to Toronto had to wait for a flight the next day after a child remained standing in a seat and would not get buckled in, the company said.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Diaz

item.title: As the Climate Warms, Beavers are Coming for Canada’s Arctic

item.title: Abbe Lane, Sultry Singer With a Latin Flair, Dies at 94

item.title: Bald Range Wildfire Forces Evacuation of 18,000 in British Columbia
